additions.site_name: ESR / CloudHQ Cosmosquare Data Centre Campus (Nanko Kita, Osaka)
additions.name: ESR－CHQ南港データセンターOS2 — planned second-phase data-centre building, Cosmosquare campus

status.summary: MLIT's register of ministerial structural-method certifications under the Building Standard Act records certification MNNNNNN-13010, dated 19 August 2026, for the building 'ESR－CHQ南港データセンターOS2' (applicant エイグ特定目的会社; evaluation by the Building Center of Japan). ESR and CloudHQ describe their Cosmosquare campus in Nanko Kita, Osaka, as three phases OS1, OS2 and OS3 that the two companies jointly build, fit out and operate, so this government record identifies the planned second-phase building on 19 August 2026 and supports announced. It is the first certification listed for OS2. A structural certification precedes building confirmation; it is not a building permit, planning consent or construction observation, and no source records OS2 works, schedule, capacity or IT load.

locator.precision: CloudHQ's published coordinate for its Cosmosquare (KIX) campus, used unchanged. It lies inside MOJ lot 南港北1丁目5-2 (the OS1 site) at its south-west corner, within 6 m of lots 5-1 and 5-3 and 8.7 m from the centroid of the three-lot street block. It locates the campus, not the OS2 building: OS2's plot, footprint and entrance are not published.
locator.identity_review: CloudHQ's KIX Campus page gives 34.63940, 135.42107 for Cosmosquare, its three-phase campus in Nanko Kita, Osaka City (phases KIX1-KIX3); ESR's releases describe the same ESR/CloudHQ Cosmosquare campus in Nanko Kita / Suminoe-ku with phases OS1-OS3, and MLIT's register names 'ESR－CHQ南港データセンターOS2'. GSI's reverse geocoder places the point in 南港北一丁目, the town block of OS1 in Osaka City's plan summary R04-035h (site 8,068.12 m2). In the 2026 MOJ registry-map data the point falls inside lot 5-2, whose planar area (8,064.3 m2) matches that site area to 0.05 %; undated Esri imagery shows a new building with dense rooftop plant filling lot 5-2 and the adjoining lot 5-3 (8,032.3 m2) cleared with temporary buildings. The point therefore marks the campus around OS1; it is not an assertion that OS2 stands on lot 5-2. Details, hashes and overlays are in the geometry-facts file.
locator.uncertainty_reason: CloudHQ publishes the point to five decimals with no datum or accuracy statement, so the decimals are not survey precision; the campus block extends about 150 m from the point and OS2's position within the campus (or on an adjoining lot) is not published.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 26 October 2026 against all five tables (sites.csv, projects.csv, evidence.csv, source-records.json, identity-mapping.json) of verified_construction_core/2026-10-26-research-seventythird and, again before finishing, 2026-10-26-research-seventyfourth (718 sites, 764 projects), all sources/*-holds.json, every queue fragment and claims.tsv, for ESR, CloudHQ, Cosmosquare/コスモスクエア, 南港/Nanko, KIX campus, OS1/OS2 and any coordinate within 2 km. No Atlas site or project lies within 2 km (nearest SoftBank Osaka Sakai 4.95 km and KDDI Osaka Sakai 5.00 km); the Atlas's MC Digital Realty KIX Campus (Saito, 26 km), whose evidence also uses the name 'KIX Campus', is a different operator and property. Within 2 km there are two holds, neither admitted: SC Zeus OSA1 (Tokyo Tatemono / SC Zeus, MOJ lot 南港北1丁目14-1, 338 m east across a street, separate developer and parcel; MLIT row '（仮称）SC Zeus 南港データセンター') and jp-kansai-p1's unpublished hold for ESR/CloudHQ Cosmosquare OS1 and the campus, which this addition creates as a site with OS2 as its only project. OS1 is not admitted (its operating statements are from 2025). The older building with rooftop plant on lot 5-1 is not identified by any source and is not attributed to ESR or CloudHQ.
additions.successor_review: MLIT's register (certifications to 30 September 2026, HTTP Last-Modified 13 October 2026) has no later OS2 row; ESR's news sitemap (captured 26 October 2026) has no Cosmosquare or OS2 item after the 2025 releases; CloudHQ's post sitemap has no Japan post and its campus page is undated; Osaka City's FY2026 building-environment-plan list (entries to R08-097) has no OS2 filing. No dated source records OS2 site works, building confirmation, construction, completion or cancellation, so the 19 August 2026 announced observation is kept. Undated imagery showing the adjoining lot 5-3 cleared is not evidence of an OS2 stage.

additions.site_name: Colt Inzai Data Centre 4 / Keppel DC REIT Tokyo Data Centre 3 (Otsuka 2-chome, Inzai)
additions.name: Colt Inzai Data Centre 4 (Keppel Tokyo Data Centre 3) — existing hyperscale data-centre operations

status.summary: Keppel DC REIT's 3Q 2026 update, published 23 October 2026, lists Tokyo Data Centre 3 in Inzai City in its portfolio overview as at 30 September 2026 with one client and 100.0% occupancy under a fully-fitted single-tenant lease, for which the owner bears all expenses and is responsible for facilities management, a 14.0-year WALE and a 2025 completion year. The REIT's Annual Report 2025 places it at 8 Otsuka 2-chome and names Colt Data Centre Services Japan Operating GK as its facility manager; it is the building Colt opened as Colt Inzai Data Centre 4 on 26 February 2025 (first phase of 4.8 MW then in operation, 20 MW planned at completion). 30 September 2026 is the reporting date, not an opening date. Occupancy is by lettable area; no IT load in use is published.

locator.precision: Planar centroid of MOJ registry-map lot 大塚二丁目8 (Inzai City), the single 8,736 m2 parcel at Keppel's stated address for Tokyo Data Centre 3 and the 8,747 m2 site of Colt Inzai Data Centre 4. It locates the data-centre property, 45 m inside its boundary; it is not the building outline, an entrance, a data hall or a surveyed point.
locator.identity_review: Keppel's Annual Report 2025 gives Tokyo Data Centre 3's location as 8 Otsuka 2-Chome, Inzai City, with 94,157 sq ft (8,747.4 m2) of land and Colt Data Centre Services Japan Operating GK as facility manager, and records its purchase from Sunrise Inzai 4 TMK. Colt's own 2023 construction-start release, Inzai 4 data sheet and timeline page give Colt Inzai Data Centre 4's site area as 8,747 m2, and Colt announced its opening in February 2025, matching Keppel's 2025 completion year and five-storey, base-isolated description. GSI returns only the 町丁目 point for 大塚二丁目8, so the '8' is a registry lot number; the 2026 MOJ/AIGID Inzai file has exactly one lot 大塚二丁目8 (H000005139, 甲二, coordinates from survey results), a single parcel of 8,735.6 m2, within 0.13% of both stated site areas. On GSI aerial tiles the lot outline follows a separate plot; the undated photo shows it vacant, so it predates construction and is not used for status. Details are in the geometry-facts file.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Registry-map accuracy class 甲二 from survey results; no parcel-specific numeric accuracy is published. The point is a parcel centroid and the property extends roughly 45-75 m from it; the building position within the lot is not measured. Seven decimals describe calculation, not survey accuracy.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 26 October 2026 against all five tables (sites.csv, projects.csv, evidence.csv, source-records.json, identity-mapping.json) of verified_construction_core/2026-10-26-research-seventythird and again of verified_construction_core/2026-10-26-research-seventyfourth (published during this work; it adds only Hong Kong sites and a Langfang refresh), every pending queue changes.json, all sources/*-holds.json and queue holds, and claims.tsv, for Colt, Keppel, Tokyo Data Centre 3, Tokyo DC 3, TDC3, Inzai 4, 印西4, 印西データセンター4, 大塚, Otsuka and Sunrise Inzai, and for any coordinate within 2 km. Existing records within 2 km: SCSK netXDC Inzai Campus (368 m; its SI3 point lies in lot 大塚二丁目5, 318 m outside lot 8, with lots 6-1, 6-2 and 7-1 between) and STT Tokyo Inzai Campus (1.50 km). Next are IIJ Shiroi (2.30 km), AirTrunk TOK1's imported Inzai locality point (3.36 km) and CloudHQ Project Asahi (3.72 km). The source-record snapshot and identity mapping have no Inzai coordinate within 2 km. The only Colt records are in Frankfurt, London and Paris; the Keppel records are in Singapore. No queue addition lies within 2 km. Holds: this resolves the Tokyo Data Centre 3 half of the q3-apac-operators-p3 lead (sixtysixth holds) and the Inzai 4 part of the jp-kanto-p1 Colt DCS Inzai campus hold (thirtysixth holds). Colt's Inzai 1-3 campus, about 600 m away according to Colt, and Inzai 5 have no address or locator and remain held; MC Digital Realty's NRT campus, held in this fragment, uses the separate Otsuka 2-chome lots 9-3, 4-1 and 4-3 (Digital Realty addresses for NRT10, NRT12 and NRT14), whose centroids are 182 m, 288 m and 252 m from lot 8's; Keppel's Tokyo Data Centres 4 and 5, also in Inzai, have no published address. One new site with one project.
additions.successor_review: Keppel DC REIT's newsroom, captured 26 October 2026 (kdcreit-news-20261026.html), lists nothing after the 23 October 3Q update except a 26 October unitholding notice; no divestment, vacancy or closure of Tokyo Data Centre 3 is reported. Colt's sitemap captured 26 October 2026 (colt-sitemap-20261026.xml) lists no 2026 Japanese press release about Inzai; the 2026 items concern appointments, the 2025 sustainability report and a Mumbai construction start. Colt's undated Inzai 4 location page (colt-ja-inzai-4.html) still carries pre-opening text that the first phase is under construction; this is superseded by Colt's February 2025 opening release and Keppel's 30 September 2026 occupancy, and it is not used for status. Later build-out beyond the first 4.8 MW phase is not established and is not inferred.

status.summary: IIJ's joint release of 26 October 2026 on a distributed quantum-computing platform, developed since 29 September 2026, states that IIJ procures, builds and operates the project's server environment at its own data centre, the Shiroi Data Center Campus in Shiroi, Chiba. This present-tense statement identifies the campus as an IIJ-operated data centre hosting current work on that date, so the existing Phase 1 and 2 operations are refreshed as operational on 26 October 2026. It gives no capacity, utilisation or new building, and the Phase 3 server building remains a separate project under construction.

status_updates.identity_review: Same facility as the existing record. IIJ has one Shiroi data-centre campus, 白井データセンターキャンパス, already in the Atlas as site vcc-site-38f7e55e7e55aaed6c27 (IIJ Shiroi Data Center Campus, bound by the Chiba registry row to 白井市桜台5-1-1) with two projects: this existing-operations record (Phases 1 and 2, operational, 7 August 2026, from IIJ's first-quarter presentation) and the Phase 3 server building (under construction, 25 June 2026). The release names the campus, not a building; current operation can only be in the existing Phase 1 and 2 buildings, because the Atlas's Phase 3 record and the thirty-fourth-update hold (citing IIJ's 7 August presentation, already Atlas evidence) place Phase 3's opening at the end of FY2026, and no completion has been reported since. The refresh keeps the record's scope and its reviewed campus locator unchanged; no phase or building is added.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 7 August 2026 observation. IIJ's 2026 press-release list captured 26 October 2026 (iij-press-2026.html) shows the 26 October release as its newest item. The releases between 7 August and 26 October (services, alliances, the 18 September MIC watt-bit demonstration naming IIJ Fukuoka Airport DC, and the 5 October Matsue disaster power-supply agreement) report no pause, closure or change at Shiroi, and no later results document is listed. The Phase 3 building is not reported complete, so the separate Phase 3 record is not touched.
